binding.later_binding_contract: classification=director_sm120_attention_split_execution_binding; exact bench_id, explicit ssh_argv, remote_root, predecessor.server_pid/start_ticks, runtime/checkpoint paths, wheel/oracle hashes, and absolute_release_deadline_utc

owner_contract.claim: A later binding is fail-closed before GpuPool construction; after admission the controller atomically claims only binding.bench_id through GpuClaimSession and binds every final release to its returned claimed_at generation.
owner_contract.staging: Only future_sm120_oracle.py is reconciled after claim by hash, temporary remote name, verify, chmod 0444, and rename. Checkpoint shards and the verified wheel are reused and are neither restaged nor rehashed.
owner_contract.predecessor: Before either oracle arm, verify the bound server PID's start ticks, stop only that process tree, prove the PID absent, and retain the captured nvidia-smi fence. A non-quiescent allocation is a retained repair boundary.
owner_contract.oracle: One parent invocation through the resident Python performs all-TRITON control followed by layer-aware FLEX_ATTENTION candidate. The owner retrieves parent stdout/stderr and every compact output, requires both arm records and path proof, and never runs the c32 endpoint.
owner_contract.repair: Each incomplete generation has a new repair_id under .repair-handshakes. The supported partial-output repair is retrieval/adoption only, so a completed control or candidate arm is not replayed; ordinary pre-submission failures remain retained behind the live claim and repair handshake.
owner_contract.release: Only a complete oracle_pass or oracle_failed terminal explicitly releases, always to maintenance with the claimed_at generation fence. Unsafe, unreachable, or elapsed absolute-deadline paths fall through the session's maintenance release.
